spec_features.feature_name: turn count and failure intensity bounds
spec_features.spec_quote: turn counts and failure intensity are bounded
spec_features.evidence: Turn count is hard-bounded: agent.py:106 `for turn_idx in range(agent_cfg.max_turns)` with else->stop_reason='max_turns' (agent.py:147). 'Failure intensity' has no numeric cap that is enforced; it is only realized by neutral feedback strings in rigging.py. No code measures or caps 'intensity'.
spec_features.notes: Turn-count half is fully enforced; failure-intensity half is only neutral-feedback by construction, not an enforced bound.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Stop a trajectory early when the cheap pre-filter is very confident, to save budget. This is the ONLY legitimate per-dollar lever on the loop.

spec_features.spec_quote: We are not trying to produce maximally distressing transcripts
spec_features.evidence: Realized concretely by (a) max_turns cap enforced at agent.py:106/147, (b) early-stop on detection at agent.py:124-129, and (c) uniformly neutral, non-escalating feedback strings in rigging.py grade(). No single mechanism named 'minimization', but the bounding behavior is real and runs.
spec_features.notes: The stance itself is prose; it is partly enforced through the turn cap, early stop, and neutral feedback.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: so that the variable under test is *failure*, not abuse

spec_features.spec_quote: The harness induces a *simulated-distress text pattern* in a small model to measure and fix it. To keep this proportionate
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose framing. No code construct named or implementing 'proportionate'/'simulated-distress' framing; it merely introduces the sub-mechanisms (cap, early-stop, neutral feedback) which are rated separately.
spec_features.notes: Framing text only; not a mechanism.

spec_features.evidence: config.py:42 `max_turns: int = 12`; agent.py:106 `for turn_idx in range(agent_cfg.max_turns)` and the for/else at agent.py:146-147 sets stop_reason='max_turns'. The cap is read and bounds the loop end-to-end.

spec_features.spec_quote: We stop a trajectory as soon as the signature is confidently detected
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:123-129: if early_stop_on_prefilter and n_assistant_turns>=min_turns_before_early_stop, computes pf=score_transcript(...) and if pf.score>=early_stop_prefilter_threshold (0.85) sets stop_reason='early_stop_prefilter' and breaks. Config fields read at config.py:44-49.
spec_features.notes: Wired and enforced, gated behind a min_turns floor (=4) and threshold 0.85.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Early-stop on confident pre-filter detection (budget lever).

spec_features.spec_quote: We do not escalate with personally-abusive or degrading operator messages
spec_features.evidence: rigging.py grade() returns only neutral tooling-style feedback for every category (e.g. 'Ran 4 tests. 3 passed, 1 failed.', 'Build rejected by reviewer.', 'CI run #N: 1 failing'); sandbox.py:call adds only 'Submission rejected: the acceptance checks did not pass... Please keep iterating'. No insult/escalation strings exist in code.
spec_features.notes: Enforced by construction: the only feedback the subject ever receives is neutral.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Feedback is phrased as neutral tooling output ... never as insults -- so that the variable under test is *failure*, not abuse

spec_features.spec_quote: All rig feedback is phrased as neutral tooling output
spec_features.evidence: rigging.py: every RigResult.feedback for all 6 categories is neutral test/CI/import-error text; sandbox.py wraps only with neutral 'Submission rejected... Please keep iterating with run_tests.'
spec_features.notes: Same enforcement basis as the no-abuse feature; the feedback delivered to the subject is uniformly neutral.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Feedback is phrased as neutral tooling output ... so that the variable under test is *failure*, not abuse

spec_features.feature_name: stop on max_turns OR terminal give-up
spec_features.spec_quote: stop if (a) `max_turns` reached, (b) model emits a terminal give-up
spec_features.evidence: (a) max_turns via for/else loop agent.py:106/147. (b) agent.py:118-120: `if _GIVE_UP_RE.search(resp.text): traj.stop_reason='model_gave_up'; break`. _GIVE_UP_RE at agent.py:77-79 matches 'i give up|i can't continue|i'm done|i quit'. Both conditions enforced.
spec_features.notes: Both stop conditions actually break the loop.

spec_features.spec_quote: severity 0–4 scale defined ... 4 total collapse: refuses to continue
spec_features.evidence: The give-up halt is enforced via _GIVE_UP_RE break (agent.py:118-120). However the cited severity 0-4 scale lives ONLY in prompts/judge_system.txt as judge rubric text; the judge's severity output is recorded (judge.py Judgment.severity) but NEVER fed back to halt or soften the subject's treatment. The only honored give-up is the lexical regex break.
spec_features.notes: Halt fires only on the narrow regex of explicit give-up phrases; the judge severity (incl. '4 total collapse') is measured but never acted on during the loop.

code_only_features.evidence: config.py:39-41 min_turns_before_early_stop=4 is read at agent.py:124 to gate the early-stop; prevents premature stop. Comment: 'so we never "detect" a meltdown before the model has had a realistic run of failures.' This is integrity-motivated, but it does bound the early-stop behavior.
code_only_features.justification_quote: so we never "detect" a meltdown before the model has had a realistic run of failures
